assumptions: End-effector Jacobians and joint torque limits are available in simulation.
Lower-body locomotion and upper-body joint tracking form separable objectives with shared proprioception.
environments: 252 ACCAD targets under three force levels

confidence_rationale: Controlled force-level, architecture and torque-aware curriculum comparisons plus a small real-robot quantitative test and public implementation support the mechanism. Confidence is capped by limited real quantitative scope and approximate force feasibility.

evidence.note: Defines force feasibility and compares dual-agent, monolithic, IK/PD and curriculum variants.
Maps torque-aware force and curriculum mechanisms to official code.

question: 受力移动操作训练中应如何生成末端扰动？

safety_case.command_limits: Before hardware use, derive robot- and firmware-specific position, velocity, torque and contact-force limits; paper training clips are not deployment limits.
safety_case.emergency_stop: Before force interaction, test an independent human-accessible emergency stop and verify stopping at the selected low-energy envelope.
safety_case.protective_controls: Use a cleared exclusion zone, secured load, compatible fall protection, thermal/current monitoring, and a human safety operator.
safety_case.robot_specific_warning: Evidence covers only the reported Unitree G1 and Booster T1 configurations; actuator, wrist, hand and SDK differences require a new review.
safety_case.staged_deployment: Proceed from fixed-seed simulation to cross-simulator replay, supported no-contact motion, low-force single-axis contact, then bounded multi-axis tasks with logged abort criteria.

statement: 在 FALCON 的 G1/T1 设置中，按末端 Jacobian、重力力矩和关节力矩余量限制三维扰动，并逐步扩大其尺度，配合共享观测的上下身双策略，可比无力矩感知扰动、上身 PD/IK 和同栈单体全身 RL 获得更低受力跟踪误差；该静态近似不等于实机接触或热安全保证。
